paper.title: From Experience to Strategy: Empowering LLM Agents with Trainable Graph Memory
paper.central_claim: Outcome-grounded FSM abstraction and reinforcement-trained utility weights produce a continually evolving graph of reusable strategies, improving fixed-model inference and guiding RL toward better generalization and efficiency.

provenance.notes: Configured sonnet→gpt-6.1-sol; independent model receipt/stable session identifier not exposed, not probed. Only own output and fixed permitted materials used; no card-member result, acceptance statistic or other-seat conclusion used as evidence.

evidence.quote:
However, these methods typically apply graph structure in a static manner and lack mechanisms to assess or refine the utility of memory components. G-Memory
(
Zhang et al., 2025
)
demonstrates how hierarchical graph-based memory can evolve by assimilating new collaborative trajectories, enabling systems to leverage cross-trial knowledge and learn from prior experiences progressively.

Pan & Zhao (2025)
focus on whether different forms of memory can enhance reasoning.
Xiong et al. (2025)
investigate long-term memory evolution.While prior memory methods often rely on static storage or task-specific designs, they lack mechanisms for evaluating and refining strategies.
In contrast, we propose a trainable graph-based memory that supports utility-aware strategy selection and reinforcement learning–driven updates, enabling generalizable and adaptive decision-making.
evidence.support_explanation: Author admits G-Memory evolves hierarchical memory, yet broadly describes prior graph memory as static. Residual difference is learned empirical strategy utility, not invention of dynamic graph memory; neighboring originals not supplied.
Paired success/failure FSM paths induce reusable strategic text. Outcome association supports induction, not proven causal diagnosis.

evidence.quote:
Meta-Cognition Update.

The memory graph is dynamically updated to preserve relevance and utility.
When a new decision path is generated, the agent evaluates its strategic value: reinforcing existing principles updates their confidence, novel patterns lead to new meta-cognition nodes, and redundant or low-confidence paths are discarded.
This selective process curates a concise set of strategic principles that evolves with experience.

The hierarchical structure thus abstracts low-level trajectories into reusable strategies.
At inference, the memory graph
𝒢
\mathcal{G}
functions as a structured policy prior guiding decision-making, while during training it provides supervision signals for reward-driven consolidation of meta-cognitive knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit new-node/confidence-update/discard curation and later inference use: persistent graph and readable strategy text, not merely model-weight training.

evidence.quote:
Effect of Disabling Weight Optimization.

We first examine the impact of freezing the memory graph weights (i.e., no learning of edge confidence). In this setup, we keep all memory edges at uniform weight and retrieve strategies purely based on structural presence. As shown in figure
4
(a)(b), performance drops significantly, particularly on
2WikiMultiHopQA
, indicating that learning to prioritize high-utility memory connections is crucial for effective strategy reuse. This validates our reinforcement-based update mechanism, which helps distinguish broadly useful meta-cognitions from less effective or overly specific ones.
evidence.support_explanation: Uniform graph-edge ablation qualitatively supports value learning; numerical curve data and uncertainty not supplied in the fixed text, so no invented effect sizes.

evidence.quote:
We exclusively use the
HotpotQA
dataset, both for model optimization and for constructing memory during the memory formation process. Evaluation is then carried out on the test or validation sets of seven diverse datasets, enabling assessment of performance both within the training domain and in out-of-domain settings.
We report
Exact Match (EM)
as the primary evaluation metric. And for memory construction in A-Mem
(
Xu et al., 2025
)
, Expel
(
Zhao et al., 2024
)
, and our proposed method, where a high-capability large language model is required, we utilized GPT-4o.

We conduct experiments on seven datasets, where HotpotQA is selected as the in-domain test set, while the remaining six datasets are used for out-of-domain evaluation. From the HotpotQA training set, we sample 1,000 examples to construct the memory and an additional 5,000 examples for weight training.

During the RL training phase, we use the rest of the HotpotQA training set as the training corpus. We adopt a batch size of 512 with a micro batch size of 64, and the rollout sampling is performed with a temperature of 1.0. To accelerate the rollout process of the LLM, we deploy vLLM v1 with a tensor parallel size of 1.

Specifically for the GRPO algorithm, the number of rollout samples (n) is set to 8. All experiments are conducted on a cluster of 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs.
evidence.support_explanation: HotpotQA-only construction, EM, common GPT-4o constructor, 1000 memory examples, additional 5000 for weight training, then ambiguous rest-of-training-set statement; GPU/batch/sampling setup but not end-to-end cost.

evidence.quote:
the number of the meta-cognition

To better understand how the quantity of retrieved meta-cognitive strategies affects agent performance, we evaluate four configurations: using 0 (no memory, denoted as ITR), 1, 3, and 5 strategies as contextual input. Results across seven QA benchmarks are presented in Table
3
.

We observe that introducing even a single meta-cognitive strategy leads to a notable improvement over the baseline (ITR), especially on multi-hop tasks such as Bamboogle (+11.6%) and HotpotQA (+2.9%). This suggests that explicit strategic signals can substantially aid reasoning even in limited quantities. As the number of strategies increases, performance generally improves, but the marginal gains become smaller—likely due to redundancy or prompt saturation. The best overall result is achieved at
top_k=5
, which balances diversity and relevance.

These findings imply that a moderate number of well-curated strategies can enhance generalization and decision quality, without incurring the risks of prompt overload or noise from irrelevant memories.
evidence.support_explanation: Appendix C.1 states best k=5, contradicting main-section k=3 optimum; Table 3 means .344/.351/.355 for k=1/3/5 support limited sensitivity, not a proved optimality/noise boundary.
Table 3 last four entries of k=5 row include 2wiki .349, Musique .094, Bamboogle .418, Avg .355: average exceeds k=3 .351, while some tasks regress.

evidence.quote:
C.2
Cross-API Memory Robustness

To further validate the portability and reliability of our structured memory graph, we construct the memory using two distinct LLM APIs:
gpt-4o
and
Gemini-2.5-pro
. These memory graphs are then integrated into the same downstream agent architecture (Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B), and evaluated across seven QA datasets. As shown in Table
4
, the resulting performance differences are minor, with Gemini-based memory slightly outperforming its 4o counterpart in most cases.

Specifically, on the multi-hop benchmark Bamboogle, the Gemini-constructed memory shows a notable increase (e.g., +0.043 on Qwen3-8B), while maintaining parity or marginal gains in general QA datasets like TriviaQA and PopQA. These results indicate that while different APIs may introduce slight variations in strategy abstraction, our framework is robust to such differences and maintains high effectiveness regardless of the underlying model used to generate the memory.
evidence.support_explanation: Appendix C.2 identifies API comparison as different memory constructors (GPT-4o/Gemini) evaluated with the same Qwen agents, rather than replacing executor while retaining identical graph.

evidence.quote:
Generalization across LLMs backends.

To evaluate whether our memory construction is tied to a specific LLM API, we replace the original
OpenAI gpt-4o
model with
Gemini-2.5-pro
and rerun the downstream evaluation using the same memory graph. As shown in Table
4
, our memory-augmented approach consistently outperforms its non-memory counterpart even under a different LLM backend, though the absolute numbers differ slightly due to model capability gaps. This demonstrates that our structured memory graph and retrieval-guided prompting strategy are largely
model-agnostic
, enabling plug-and-play use across modern foundation models.
evidence.support_explanation: Main section instead describes changing API with same graph. This conflicts with appendix constructor protocol; claim of broad plug-and-play transfer must be narrowed.

evidence.quote:
The induction of meta-cognitions is accomplished through three primary analytical scenarios, each facilitated by a dedicated prompt:

Intra-Query Analysis: This involves comparing successful and failed trajectories that originate from the identical query to distill a high-confidence causal principle. The prompt for this process is presented in
E.3
.

Inter-Query Analysis: This contrasts a failed trajectory with successful ones from semantically similar but distinct queries to generate speculative heuristics.

Positive Example Distillation: This process extracts generalizable strategies exclusively from a collection of successful execution paths.
evidence.support_explanation: Appendix adds positive-only distillation, whereas Algorithm 1 returns empty if only successes. This is an implementation/protocol ambiguity, not proof the program failed.

No independent reproduction; no improver label: no changed-improver generating better future edits under comparable budgets.
Main/appendix disagreements over positive-only induction, k optimum and API comparison; precise utility-training split and test dedup not supplied.
Neighbor originals and numerical plot pixels/uncertainty not available in fixed manifest.

G.reason: Concrete residual issue is utility-aware selection of structured experience, not static-vs-dynamic memory generally. G-Memory and other evolving stores are admitted but originals missing; independent novelty/need versus cheaper abstraction remains open.

M.reason: Three-layer query→FSM path→strategy and guided/unguided REINFORCE credit produce a reconstructable, falsifiable selection mechanism. Distinct from similarity-only recall; sampled credit noise and multi-strategy interactions limit a stronger causal guarantee.

X.reason: Memory writes/reads and ranking objective explicit, but full FSM transition table not concretely instantiated in prompt, numerical hyperparameters/reward details/loop schedule incomplete; positive-only induction, optimal k and API protocol conflict. No reliable decay/version/rollback.

E.measurement.reason: Named QA benchmarks, common Wikipedia/E5 and exact match give interpretable measurements with reconstructable averages. EM sensitivity to answer specificity is shown in Appendix D; per-test denominators and fuller verifier-normalization audit absent, so no maximal validity claim.

E.causality.reason: Inference separates persistent memory from executor training, compares raw/abstract memory alternatives and reports uniform-edge removal; RL has weights-only and memory variants. Missing matched budgets and factorized FSM/curator/utility controls leave extra compute and abstraction explanations.

E.holdout.reason: Declared HotpotQA training construction with six other QA evaluation sets supports retained transfer. No audited overlap/utility-update split, unclear 5000-versus-rest training allocation and API protocol limit broader unseen-domain/model claims; no proven test-label use is alleged.

E.statistics.reason: 1000 memory and 5000 training sample counts plus task/baseline regressions give a minimal denominator/boundary report; evaluation n and main-run uncertainty are not stated. No described seeds/intervals/stream-order repetitions. No unseen figure error-bar inference.
search_scope: Entire fixed text lines 1–5371, main results/ablation descriptions, Appendices A–E and all text tables/captions; no page_images supplied.

E.cost.reason: Hardware, batch/rollout setup and six-tool-call cap are coarse resource context only. No full teacher, counterfactual-graph, inference-token or RL time/cost accounting and no matched total budget. Paired utility requires two trajectories by design.
search_scope: Sections 4–5, Appendices A–E, Algorithms1–2; hardware/setup reported but end-to-end costs not quantified.

reason: 完整材料可判：固定模型推理独立展示持久外部图/策略的后续收益，故为范围内A类而非纯参数训练。保留作者广义持续演化/泛化/效率主张，窄化到所报告QA留存收益；协议矛盾、缺强归因与成本/统计限制评分，不改卡片或rubric。
rationale: 成败FSM对比形成留存策略图，配对奖励学习边权；固定模型QA有后续收益。缺同预算强归因与统计，k最优值、API迁移及正例分支表述矛盾，广义持续演化和效率未充分成立。
